episode_summary: Episode 280 (October 2019) opens with a roundtable on whether Bitcoin could go to zero, covering the MySpace versus Facebook network-effect analogy, whether Lightning works for real payments, QR code adoption, and Wayne's FedCoin thesis. The main interview is with Norman Moore of Lightning in a Box about building cheap Raspberry Pi, Odroid and BTCPay Lightning nodes and the design of Casa's node.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Colin said he had sold all his crypto at around $10K after finally breaking even.
cards.speaker: Colin
cards.quote: I just sold all my coins. I just sold everything.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Colin argued that Bitcoin and Ethereum technology could not support the vision people were pushing, so the price should fall.
cards.speaker: Colin
cards.quote: So the technology cannot support the vision that people are trying to push.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said Bitcoin was straight up GeoCities and Ethereum was at the MySpace level of network effects.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: Bitcoin is straight up geocities when it comes to like what this

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said Nakamoto consensus is memory heavy, needing a lot of space and syncing to run a full node.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: Well, not state heavy, it's memory heavy. It requires a lot of space, a lot of syncing

cards.claim: In October 2019 the roundtable debated whether Bitcoin, unlike MySpace, keeps its value when users leave, since users who leave a social network lose nothing but a Bitcoin holder keeps monetary value.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: However, crypto is different, Bitcoin especially, in that if I get off MySpace, I didn't lose anything.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said he would not make a claim that Bitcoin will not go to zero, admitting he did not know.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: I'm not going to sit here and make a claim that Bitcoin isn't going to go to zero. I don't know.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said Bitcoin is likely never going to reach absolute zero, and that it was unlikely to go to zero in their lifetime.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: And if you ask me if it's going to zero, the answer is likely no.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said Bitcoin was overvalued and overhyped for global payment systems, which needed a layer 2 solution that caused user experience problems.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: I do think it's overvalued and overhyped for what you're trying to do when they talk about things like global payment systems

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said the Lightning Network worked well for small purchases, such as a five-dollar coffee, with payments of ten dollars and under working well.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: you're supposed to buy your coffee on the lightning network a five dollar purchase

cards.claim: In October 2019 the roundtable debated whether Bitcoin, like MySpace, is a company, with one side saying it is a community, and that early telephone and TCP/IP systems faced the same criticisms.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: if Bitcoin were a company like MySpace or something, I would agree with you. But Bitcoin is a community.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said a global payment system cannot be solved with the constraints of a store of value.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: And a global payment system cannot be solved with the constraints that come with a store of value.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest predicted QR codes would never take off in the United States.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: QR codes have been trying to take off and nothing is going to get them to take off

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said his grandmother's generation would be gone and her grandchildren would be using QR codes for payments instead of checks.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: Your grandma's going to die and her grandkids are going to be using QR codes.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Wayne said a properly executed FedCoin would be a major threat to Bitcoin's value.
cards.speaker: Wayne
cards.quote: And that would be a a properly executed Fed coin, one where the government actually got their stable, quote-unquote, coin.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Wayne said a FedCoin that airdrops to crypto users, provides universal basic income and is used to pay taxes would mean Bitcoin is dead, and predicted a smaller country would do it first.
cards.speaker: Wayne
cards.quote: They required you to pay your taxes with it. Those three things, Bitcoin is dead.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a host said he paid for a refrigerator magnet with Lightning through BTCPay Server in about three seconds.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: i bought a refrigerator magnet for four dollars and some odd cents and that

cards.claim: Norman Moore said he built an Ethereum mining rig in spring 2016 after a hunch about Ethereum.
cards.speaker: Norman Moore
cards.quote: But I got a bug again back in spring of 2016 and I had a hunch about ethereum

cards.claim: Norman Moore said his first Lightning node was built on an Odroid HC2 with a 2.5-inch drive attached.
cards.speaker: Norman Moore
cards.quote: using an Odroid HC2, which was a little computer that has a SATA connection.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Norman Moore said his early Lightning node was roughly one of the top 300 nodes online on mainnet, when Eclair had about 500 Android downloads.
cards.speaker: Norman Moore
cards.quote: I think Eclair at the time had maybe 500 downloads on the Android app, and I was maybe in the top 300 first nodes to come online with that on the mainnet.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Norman Moore said the Raspberry Pi 4 finally made it sensible to run a Lightning or Bitcoin node on a Raspberry Pi.
cards.speaker: Norman Moore
cards.quote: now suddenly we have something that makes sense to run a Raspberry, to run a node on

cards.claim: In October 2019 Norman Moore said a Breeze wallet let users spend over Lightning within a few minutes of dropping Bitcoin on it, running on Neutrino.
cards.speaker: Norman Moore
cards.quote: there's a Breeze wallet that's fairly seamless. You drop Bitcoin on it, and you have a lightning spend capability within a few minutes that runs on Neutrino.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Norman Moore said a Raspberry Pi 4 with an SSD could sync a full Bitcoin node in about two and a half days, versus over a month on a Pi 3.
cards.speaker: Norman Moore
cards.quote: The Raspberry Pi 4 with an SSD will sink in about two and a half days, start to finish.

cards.claim: Norman Moore said Casa's first node iteration was hard to use, as average buyers struggled to open router ports.
cards.speaker: Norman Moore
cards.quote: so its first iteration was a little hard to use in my opinion

cards.claim: In October 2019 Norman Moore described Bitcoin on the base layer as a savings account and Lightning on top as a checking account.
cards.speaker: Norman Moore
cards.quote: Right now, Bitcoin on a base layer is a savings account. On Lightning, it's a checking account.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Wayne predicted there would be a consolidated global FedCoin, and that it was inevitable.
cards.speaker: Wayne
cards.quote: There will be not only individual Fed coins, but there will be a consolidated global Fed coin.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said it only takes about four phone calls to the miners or pool operators to reverse a Bitcoin transaction.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: it only takes like four phone calls to completely reverse a transaction

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said he would move to a better coin if it had network effect, but had not yet seen one.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: If there was a better coin, I'd move. And it had the network effect, I'd move. But I haven't seen it yet.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said the crypto industry had an oligarchy in Bitcoin, Ethereum and crypto generally.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: we have an oligarchy in bitcoin we have an oligarchy in ethereum

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest put Bitcoin's total market value at about 150 billion dollars.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: no it's not even triple digit billions anymore 150 billion

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #280: Norm -- Lightning in a Box
